panels.title: Total Power Now
panels.description: Sum of every metered plug. The HP Elite mini PC has no plug and is NOT counted.

panels.title: Burn Rate
panels.description: USD/hour at the current draw and the current TOU rate.

panels.title: Billable Draw
panels.description: Total draw minus the solar-fed shed. This is what the cost figures price.

panels.title: Rate Now ($/kWh)
panels.description: All-in marginal rate: (energy + delivery riders) x (1 + tax).

panels.title: Run-Rate / Year
panels.description: Annualised from the CURRENT instant billable draw — a what-if, not a forecast.

panels.title: Hot spots — who is costing what
Biggest Draw Right Now
panels.description: Name of the highest-drawing plug, with its wattage.

panels.title: Live Draw — Per Plug
panels.description: Sorted by draw. This is the hot-spot list.

panels.title: Cost Last Month
panels.description: The finished total for the previous calendar month, from utility_meter's last_period. Unlike Cost This Month it no longer moves.

panels.title: This Month vs Last
panels.description: Month-to-date minus last month's finished total. Negative early in the month is normal — it only means the month is young, not that costs fell.

panels.title: Cost Last Month — Per Device
panels.description: Last month's finished cost, per device.

panels.title: Cost / Year If Left At This Draw
panels.description: What each device would cost over a year if it never left its current draw. Solar-fed plugs read zero by design. Sizes the payback of turning something off; it is not a bill forecast.

panels.title: Idle floor — what it costs to do nothing
Idle Floor (24h min)
panels.description: Lowest total draw in 24h — the always-on baseline you pay for even when nothing runs.

panels.title: Baseline Cost / Year
panels.description: The idle floor, annualised. This is the number that only shrinks by removing or consolidating hardware.

panels.title: Headroom Above Idle
panels.description: Peak minus idle: how much of the draw is actual work vs. just being powered on.

panels.title: Total vs Billable vs Idle Floor
Energy Today — Per Plug (resets at midnight)
Voltage
panels.description: Real plugs only — the estimated host reports no electrical telemetry.

panels.title: Current
panels.description: Real plugs only — the estimated host reports no electrical telemetry.

options.content:
### Where the money actually goes

**Idle floor is the real bill.** Peak draw is dramatic but brief; the 24h minimum runs 8,760
hours a year. If *Baseline Cost / Year* is most of *Cost This Year*, no amount of workload
tuning helps — only removing or consolidating a box does.

**Hot-spot triage, in order:**

1. **Threadripper host** is the swing consumer. It idles high (big PSU, HDDs, one RTX 3090) and
   spikes under inference. Check it against `docs/domains/ai-gpu/gpu-scale-swap.md` — the GPU
   workloads are mutually exclusive whole-card allocations, so a backend left at `replicas: 1`
   with nothing calling it is pure idle cost. `POWER_LIMIT_WATTS` caps the card's ceiling.
2. **HP SFF + Optiplex share one plug.** A high reading here cannot be attributed to either box.
   Split the outlet before drawing conclusions about which one to retire.
3. **NAS Drive PSU vs TrueNAS Server** are two plugs on one machine — spinning disks vs the
   host. Persistent draw on the drive PSU with an idle host means spindles that never sleep.
4. **Gaming PC** is a workstation, not a cluster node. It is metered but deliberately NOT
   power-locked, so it is expected to swing between zero and several hundred watts.

**Two numbers here are not measurements:**

- **HP Elite (est.)** has no smart plug. Its draw is a flat assumed figure set by
  `input_number.hp_elite_estimated_watts` in Home Assistant, so it moves the totals without
  ever reflecting reality. Fit a plug and the guess goes away.
- **Shed is solar-fed**, so its cost rate is pinned to zero: it contributes watts and kWh but
  no dollars, and *Billable Draw* is total draw minus the shed. What its own supply is doing —
  MPPT yield, battery bank state of charge — is on the **Solar MPPT Monitor** dashboard.

**Numbers that are what-ifs, not forecasts:** *Run-Rate / Year* and *Cost / Year If Left At This
Draw* annualise the current instant. They answer "what does leaving this on cost me?" — they are
not a prediction of next month's bill. Use *Cost This Month* for that.

**Cost basis:** the all-in marginal rate — (energy + delivery riders) x (1 + sales tax) — which
steps between summer on-peak, summer off-peak and non-summer. Rates live in
`my-apps/home/home-assistant/configuration.yaml` under `input_number:`; git is the source of
truth and the UI sliders reset to it on restart.
